title: Multiscale continuous batcher and KV lifecycle optimization for mixed-length prompt/response workloads
creator: Asha Patel
description: Tuning the continuous-batching scheduler for mixed prompt/response lengths by introducing a multiscale coalescing layer and a KV lifecycle manager. Goal: reduce 95th percentile token latency for mixed dialogue workloads while preserving or improving GPU utilization and overall throughput. Approach combines time-windowed micro-coalescing, adaptive slot-shepherding to avoid head-of-line blocking, and proactive KV pin/evict policies tied to turn affinity and predicted continuation probability.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 95th percentile per-token latency for mixed prompt/response benchmark <= 120ms on p4d-8x with default runtime settings; 2) End-to-end throughput >= baseline or within -5% while reducing average GPU memory fragmentation by >= 10%; 3) No regression in unit tests and CI smoke pipelines; 4) Can be toggled with a feature flag and safely rolled back.
progress_updates: 2025-02-10: Ticket created after spike showed tail-latency bursts on mixed-turn chat workloads. Initial hypothesis: long responses and short prompts are being coalesced into inefficient slots causing KV churn and GPU slab fragmentation.

2025-02-14: Spike completed (microbench harness) - implemented prototype 'slot-shepherd' scheduler and multiscale coalescer. Observed 12% improvement in mean token throughput and unstable 95th percentile (improved in some runs, regressed in others). Recorded traces and flame graphs.

2025-02-20: Design review with runtime and infra teams. Decided to separate concerns: (A) multiscale coalescer (time windows: micro 2-5ms, meso 8-25ms, macro 50-150ms) and (B) KV lifecycle manager responsible for pin/soft-evict heuristics based on turn affinity and continuation probability models.
2025-02-26: Implemented KV lifecycle manager prototype with pinning TTL and hot-turn scoring. Added telemetry hooks for KV-hit-rates, eviction counts, and slab-redistribution events.

2025-03-03: Canary on staging: Enabled feature flag for 10% of traffic on dedicated GPU pool. Observed 18% reduction in average GPU memory fragmentation metric and 9% decrease in total KV evictions, but 95th percentile latency still intermittently spikes when long responses align with large incoming prompt bursts.

2025-03-08: Added adaptive-preemption: scheduler can preempt and split late-arriving long responses into separate slots if they would increase tail latency. Preliminary runs show fewer spikes but slight throughput drop (~3%).
2025-03-12: Running extended A/B several-hour test with synthetic and production-like traffic. Collected end-to-end traces; preparing PR and rollout notes.
Blockers: Need final approval for new telemetry retention policy (storage budget) from Observability team and a perf budget exception for staging experiments from Platform SRE.
decisions: Adopted multiscale coalescing windows rather than single global latency threshold to capture both micro-bursts and sustained traffic mixes.
KV lifecycle manager will use soft-evict with grace windows and a small pinned-reservation for 'continuation-affine' turns to reduce re-warm cost.
Introduced adaptive-preemption to split long responses into separate slots if they threaten to push 95th latency above target during the window.
Feature gated changes behind runtime.feature.multiscale_batcher and runtime.feature.kv_lifecycle for safe rollout/rollback.
experiment_results: Staging synthetic mix (60% short prompts, 40% long responses): mean token latency -8%, p95 token latency -14% in stable runs, throughput +6%.

Production-like replay run: GPU memory fragmentation metric down 18%, KV eviction rate down 9%, but p95 showed intermittent +25% spikes before adaptive-preemption; after preemption spikes reduced to +3% compared to baseline.
Cost impact estimate: net inference token cost unchanged or slightly improved due to fewer cache reloads; CPU overhead for scheduler up ~1.5%.
Telemetry indicates better KV locality for multi-turn sessions (session KV hit-rate +11%).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-pin of KV entries could starve slab space causing OOMs on noisy neighbors. Mitigation: conservative TTL defaults, dynamic pressure monitor that converts pins to soft-evict under slab pressure.
Risk: Adaptive-preemption might reduce batching efficiency harming throughput. Mitigation: aggressive rollout gating (canary percentage) and step-down policies when throughput drops >5%.
Risk: Increased scheduler CPU could affect tail latency. Mitigation: offload heavy heuristics to a sampled path and keep hot-path decision as lightweight as possible.
Risk: Telemetry storage growth. Mitigation: retention tiering and sample-based trace collection; coordinated review with Observability team (see blockers).
testing_plan: Unit tests for slot-shepherd decisions and KV lifecycle scoring.
Integration tests in the microbench harness with deterministic random seeds.
Long-running soak tests on staging under production-replay traffic for 48 hours.
A/B rollout: 0% -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback triggers for p95 regression and OOM signals.
Chaos test: induce KV slab pressure and verify graceful demotion of pinned entries.
Perf bench: run the standard Mixed-Turn benchmark and compare token-latency distributions (p50/p90/p95/p99) against baseline.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flags; 2) Canary 1% on dedicated pool for 24h; 3) Increase to 10% with monitoring for 6h; 4) 50% with health gates; 5) Full rollout if no regressions. Rollback: flip feature flags and revert PR if any critical alerts (OOM, p95 > 120ms for >15min, KV eviction rate spike >30%).
owner_notes: Follow-up task: train a lightweight continuation probability model using recent session traces (ENG-439000 planned).
Coordinate with Observability to add KV-hot-turn dashboards and slab-heatmaps.
Post-rollout: schedule a blameless incident retro if we observe unexpected memory behavior.
